newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: SOCCER-LATE PENALTY GIVES YUGOSLAVIA A POINT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE PENALTY GIVES YUGOSLAVIA A POINT.

text.p: - A penalty three minutes from time gave Yugoslavia a 1-1 World Cup qualifying draw with Spain on Wednesday to keep alive the battle for top spot in group six.
Spain led with a 19th minute penalty by Fernando Hierro and were kept in the game by keeper Andoni Zubizaretta until Predrag Mijatovic converted the late spot kick.
Spain still tops the group with 17 points, one ahead of Yugoslavia with Slovakia also still very much in contention on 12 points with two games in hand.
After a cautious start Spain's first real attack paid dividends when Sinisa Mihajlovic brought down Kiko Narvaez in the box and Hierro duly converted.
The Yugoslavs thought they should have had a penalty in the 26th minute when Miguel Nadal clattered into Dejan Savicevic in the Spanish box but the referee awarded only an indirect free kick.
It was the spur for sustained home pressure with veteran Zubizaretta making three good saves within three minutes.
Dragan Stojkovic scraped a post and Mihajlovic tested Zubizaretta with a long-distance free kick as the hosts continued to press.
In the second half Spanish coach Javier Clemente sought to protect his lead by introducing three more defensive players as the Yugoslavs boosted their forward line.
Injury-plagued AC Milan star Dejan Savicevic had to be replaced after only 36 minutes but Yugoslavia attacked relentlessly in the second half.
Zubizaretta was again to the fore but there were also some bad misses.
Just when it seemed the Spaniards would hold out, substitute Juan Lopez brought down Dejan Govedarica in the box and Real Madrid's Mijatovic made no mistake from the spot.
Fans were overjoyed to see Mijatovic on the scoresheet after the Spanish-based player was relentlessly jeered by the Valencia crowd in Spain 2-0 defeat of Yugoslavia last year.
Yugoslav coach Slobodan Santrac said: "The team played exceptionally well. We had our chances but you also need some luck, and we didn't have that today.
"I think this was an important point. We can now realistically look forward to going to France," he added.
Yugoslavia have previously beaten Spain at three foreign venues but had never even scored against them at home.
They now face two make-or-break games against Slovakia.
For Spain, now unbeaten in 27 games, it was a satisfactory point and they should go on to qualify for France 98.
While taking a corner Spain's Josep Guardiola was apparently hit on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from the stands. The referee took no action but FIFA might.
Lineups:

Yugoslavia: Ivica Kralj, Zoran Mirkovic, Goran Djorovic, Risto Vidakovic (Zeljko Petrovic 46), Miroslav Djukic, Sinisa Mihajlovic, (Dragan Ciric 79), Dejan Govedarica, Dejan Savicevic (Savo Milosevic 36), Predrag Mijatovic, Dragan Stojkovic, Ljubinko Drulovic.

Spain - Andoni Zubizaretta, Abelardo Fernandez, Sergi Barjuan, Rafael Alkorta, Miguel Nadal, Fernando Hierro, Kiko Narvaez (Luis Enrique 55), Roberto Rios (Juan Lopez 57), Josep Guardiola, Raul Gonzales, Perez Alfonso (Guillermo Amor 68).
